Declared next to the -webkit-line-clamp/-webkit-box fallback, which browsers without unprefixed line-clamp still honor.
Only used inside :is() (forgiving selector list), so a browser without :state() drops that one alternative; the .selected / [aria-selected] alternatives still match.

These rules only style ::view-transition-* pseudo-elements, which exist only while a view transition runs; a browser without the API never matches them (an unknown pseudo-element drops just that rule).
The declaration is dropped where calc-size() is unsupported and the adjacent @supports not (inline-size: calc-size(...)) branch supplies the clip-path fallback (fab-menu.scss).

The icon registrations are ignored where @property is unsupported; every var() in md-icon.scss repeats the registered initial value as its fallback, so icons render the same and only the animated fill change jumps.
Treated as scroll where unsupported (iOS Safari): each skeleton block pulses its own slice of the band instead of one shared viewport band; the placeholder color and animation still render.

Ignored where CSS d is unsupported: the SVG path keeps its d attribute (the initial/flat or wavy shape from the markup), so a visible indicator is drawn; only the shape morph and amplitude transition are lost.

An unsupported style() query drops only its own rule; list.scss sets the same segmented color and first/last item radii through plain custom properties (--_segmented-container-color, --_first-child-radius) before it.
An unsupported style() query drops only its own rule; the element sets .progress-wave-amplitude for the same range, which applies the same wavy shape.
Without @property the --ripple-* values still apply (:where(.ripple) sets the same initial values) but change without animating; the state layers stay visible.

Without @property the animated --_md-progress-* values still resolve (:where(.progress) sets the same initial values) and determinate progress is exact; the indeterminate animation steps instead of interpolating.

An unsupported style() query drops only its own rule: menu.scss writes every one of them a second time from the same mixin under :where(.menu-vibrant, .menu-vibrant *) / :where(.menu-grouped, .menu-grouped *), and md-gb-menu-item / md-gb-menu-group put those classes on their root, so vibrant items and grouped surfaces render the same without style queries.
